roof:
Use case: historical-scene
Asset: modular roof sprite atlas for Water Margin RPG, Northern Song dynasty China around 1120.
Precisely 6 columns x 4 rows, square cells, no gaps, no margins, no labels or grid lines. Logical native canvas96x64 pixels, each cell16x16. Hard-edged chunky pixel art, top-down three-quarter JRPG view as Suikoden II, muted earthy palette8–16 colors per tile. If rendered larger keep the same extremely simple logical pixels with nearest-neighbor enlargement. Transparent outside roof silhouette.
Rows1–2 contain two complete roofs next to each other: columns1–3 ordinary grey tube-tiled town house roof; columns4–6 straw thatched village roof.
Rows3–4: columns1–3 dark charcoal-grey tiled temple/official hall roof with restrained upward ends; columns4–6 weathered warm grey tiled roof for a red-timber shrine.
For each3x2 roof, top row is ridge and upper slope, bottom row lower slope and eave; columns are left end, seamless repeatable middle, right end. Roofs connect exactly at cell edges. Upper slope tiles must fill bottom boundary; lower slope tiles fill top boundary. Center tiles must repeat horizontally without borders. Show rows of cylindrical clay tube tiles and shallow channels, broad gently sloping roofs, structural timber brackets under eave, historically restrained ornaments.
Northern Song silhouette based on Yingzao Fashi, not Ming/Qing palaces: NO yellow roofs, no ornate dragon swarms, no aggressive hornlike corners, no multistorey pagoda, no Japanese torii, no modern objects. Thatch has NO curved tile ornaments. Roofs only, no walls or ground. Strict sprite sheet, not scene or showcase.
